esc-028-verify-fields.reason: Granted by Hank 2026-09-05 ('Approved. Go for it.') on ESC-028. Repoint a ticket's verify field at a grader that ALREADY EXISTS, is merged, and has been measured. Never to invent a gate, never to point a gate at a test chosen because it passes, and never any other field of the ticket graph. The narrowness is the grant: 143 of 296 tickets carry the NO-GATE placeholder while real graders exist for some of them, which leaves done work unbankable and ready work undispatchable for the same one-line reason. NOTE, because INSIDE must not be read as harmless here: `verify` is not an inert value, it IS the gate red-check executes, so a structurally-INSIDE delta can still be a substantively bad one. INSIDE means only that the delta touched no other field. Every use of this class states the grader it points at and the measurement that shows the grader exists and runs.

esc-029-status-correction.reason: Granted by Hank 2026-09-06 ('if there's anything else that you need overridden, let me know right now', and 'put those in the prompt as well... all of your hopes, dreams, and desires, put them all into a prompt so I can have one agent do all of it'). Correct a ticket's `status` field ONLY where the recorded status is demonstrably FALSE -- specifically, where a ticket is recorded closed while its own defect STILL REPRODUCES on the current tree. Every use must record the MEASUREMENT that proves the defect reproduces: the command run and its output, taken at the head being judged. The status moves to reflect reality, never the reverse. THIS IS NOT PERMISSION TO CLOSE TICKETS, and that is the limit that matters: marking something closed because it looks done is the exact move this class forbids, so a status edit TOWARD closed is outside it however plausible the work looks -- closure is earned through the gate, not through this grant. It touches no other field of the ticket graph. THE LIVE CASE IT WAS GRANTED FOR: T-150 is recorded `status: closed`, yet its node still carries a strict xfail marker and still genuinely fails under `--runxfail` -- a served auction driven end-to-end through `exchange.main.create_app()` puts no event into the trust ledger by any channel. A ticket recorded closed whose defect reproduces is a false green in the ledger itself, which is the one place a false green cannot be caught by re-running the suite.

esc-031-evidence-restatement.reason:
Granted by Hank 2026-09-06 as esc-031-evidence-restatement, the third of the standing ticket-graph classes. tickets.json `status_evidence` FIELD ONLY. It exists because a survey of the 168 recorded status_evidence strings found the majority of them ASSERTING AS PRESENT-TENSE FACT things the tree contradicts: paths recorded as "does not exist" or "is a 0-byte __init__.py" that hold tens of thousands of bytes of code, paths recorded "untouched since <sha>" that git shows 1-32 commits on, tickets recorded "no commit names it" that up to 28 commits name, and -- the sharpest -- cited LINE NUMBERS that have drifted onto the comment DESCRIBING THE REPAIR, so the evidence now reads as confirmation of a defect while quoting its fix. That is a false green in the ledger, in the one field no test parses and therefore the one field no re-run can catch.

THE BINDING CONDITION, which must be honoured in every edit made under this class: Every restated clause carries `measured at <sha>:`. An undated "does not exist" is believed forever; a stamped one announces its own age. A restatement without a sha is OUTSIDE this class even though it touches only the whitelisted field -- the class permits correcting evidence, not minting a fresh undated snapshot that begins decaying at the next close(...) commit.

WHAT IT DOES NOT PERMIT. It does NOT permit editing `status`: that field is covered by esc-029-status-correction and by that class ONLY IN ONE DIRECTION -- toward open, where a ticket recorded closed still reproduces its own defect -- so a `status` move cannot be smuggled in alongside an evidence correction here. It does not permit ADDING or REMOVING tickets: the id set and the ticket order must come out of a restatement byte-identical, and every use of this class proves that structurally (both versions parsed, order compared, id set compared, every field of every ticket compared one by one) rather than by eye. It touches no other field of the ticket graph -- not `verify`, not `scope`, not `acceptance`.

AND IT IS NOT A LICENCE TO SAY THE WORK IS DONE. A corrected evidence string states what was MEASURED at the named sha and nothing more. Where a measurement contradicts the old claim but does not establish the ticket's true state, the restatement must SAY SO in the evidence rather than guess -- "the cited line no longer says this" is a finding; "therefore the ticket is fixed" is a closure, and closure is earned through the gate, never through this grant.
